impact:
Blocks Python-free CI (and therefore the published package's CI, and the repo after usage.py retires). Deferred from T-005 because one ticket carrying the registry migration AND the artifact pipeline was unreviewable — a defect in the migration would be indistinguishable from an artifact-pipeline defect in one review.

Design is preserved in .story/sessions/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000/plan.md section 5.1, after six review rounds. The load-bearing conclusion, which three earlier designs got wrong:

An artifact payload and its digest index emitted by the SAME generator in one operation are NOT semantically verified — they are only internally consistent. A generator bug that mis-associates argv, captures the wrong stream or substitutes the wrong token produces a matching-BAD pair, and regenerating with that same generator reproduces it deterministically. So the ticket requires a verifier that imports NOTHING from the generator and re-derives from fake_ccusage.py directly.

Also settled: canonical rendering (a "sha256 of rendered bytes" is undefined against a randomly allocated temp HOME, so digests are stored for a canonical /fixture/home substitution); separate stdoutSha256 and stderrSha256, never concatenated, because ("ab","c") and ("a","bc") collide; a termination object rather than a bare exit; staleness checks covering stored goldens and not just fixtures/; and an AUTHORED invocation inventory, since instrumenting the fake only discovers argv for whatever the generator happened to run.

Honest bound to carry forward: pure conformance catches one-sided corruption and consumer defects; only the independent verifier catches a bad artifact PAIR. Publication must therefore require the verifier.
title: T-005a: deterministic fixture artifacts + an INDEPENDENT oracle verifier
